1.explanation:
We render two instances of the Carbon NumberInput to trigger the DAP rules:

• First instance (disabled):
  – disabled=true keeps the invalid icon in the DOM with role="img" but no alt text.
  – Running DAP on this instance flags the missing non-empty alternative text for the widget with IMG role.

• Second instance (validation + hideLabel):
  – invalid=true shows the invalid icon and error text, hideLabel=true visually hides the label but leaves it in the DOM.
  – The input’s accessible name is pulled from the ariaLabel prop (default “Numeric input field with increment and decrement buttons”), not matching the visible label text.
  – DAP flags “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label text.”

You can drop this code into a Create React App or Storybook environment with carbon-components-react v10+ and run DAP (e.g. the IBM Accessibility extension) to reproduce both violations.
1.bug_scenario:
There are two distinct accessibility violations when rendering the Carbon React NumberInput component:

1. Disabled state violation
   • Render the NumberInput with the disabled prop.  
   • The invalid icon (<svg> with role="img") used internally to indicate an invalid state is still in the DOM even when disabled, and it has a role="img" but no alt text or aria-label. DAP flags this as “WAI-ARIA widget with IMG role must have a non-empty alternate text or a label.”

2. Form-validation/label mismatch violation
   • Render the NumberInput in a validation state with a visible label but also pass hideLabel and rely on the ariaLabel prop (which defaults to “Numeric input field with increment and decrement buttons”).  
   • Because the visible label text (“Number Input label”) is visually hidden but still present in the DOM, and the input’s accessible name is taken exclusively from the ariaLabel prop, DAP flags “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label text.”
